A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Conditional Balance work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices. Existing material can be matched despite additions, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, layer-selection and geometric-control analyses, quantitative comparisons in Table 2, and a 42-participant user study in Table 1.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds SD3.5 experiments, a reversed-ranking ablation, Gram-matrix evaluation, and additional application and failure examples.

M1.justification: v2 Appendix C adapts stylization to SD3.5 joint attention: normalization and feature sharing occur before concatenation with text features, and AdaIN additionally operates on Value projections. This extends the conditioning procedure while retaining the original sensitivity-ranking algorithm and SDXL method.

E1.justification: v2 adds photographic-editing styles, an unfamiliar-artist failure scenario, and ReStyle/ReContent examples that modify artwork content while preserving its structure (Sections 11.2, 11.5 and 12.3). The original 32-style benchmark remains unchanged; SD3.5 itself is a model extension rather than new task coverage.

E2.justification: The new style-layer ablation adds least-sensitive-layer selection as a comparator alongside sensitive and random selections (v2 Figure 13). The named external baseline set is unchanged, including RB-Modulation and InstaStyle, which already appeared in v1's appendix.

E3.justification: v2 adds Gram-matrix style scoring alongside DINO and evaluates SD3.5 with conditioning on 28 of 38 joint-attention layers. The original benchmark and user-study protocols remain unchanged. The revised B-LoRA wording specifying 10 self-attention layers agrees with v1's appendix, which already distinguished these from 20 layers including cross-attention.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens diagnostic validation through a reversed-ranking ablation, an alternative-style-descriptor check, transfer of painting-derived layer selections to photographic styles, and an unfamiliar-style failure analysis (Figures 13 and 17–19). The original layer-count and geometric-control analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The generation seeds, five analysis repetitions, layer-rank mean and standard-deviation reporting, and user-study chi-squared analysis remain unchanged. The added experiments introduce no new uncertainty-reporting or statistical-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and all retained figure results are unchanged. v2 substantially extends the findings with reversed-ranking curves, Gram-matrix comparison scores, SD3.5 outcomes, photographic-style results, editing examples and an unfamiliar-style failure. These are additional results under new controls, metrics or scenarios.

T1.justification: The Gaussian feature representation, stated divergence, within- and between-cluster distances, and ranking ratio in Equations 1–4 are unchanged. The additions introduce no new mathematical definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction's three contributions remain essentially unchanged. v2 modestly broadens the method's stated scope beyond SDXL self-attention through its explicit joint-attention applicability claim and the conclusion's more general reference to attention layers.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the SDXL-only architectural limitation with a limitation tied to the base model's knowledge of the requested style, illustrated using Enfant Précoce. It also interprets insensitive-layer stylization as interfering with content. The original explanation of content/style over-conditioning is retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents the SD3.5 conditioning adaptation and layer setting, and supplies ReStyle/ReContent instructions using Canny or Depth maps with approximately 0.55 style weight and content weight below 0.2. It also updates the project-page address; code and evaluation-set availability were already stated in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to SD3, Cross-Image Attention, LooseControl, ZEST and SmartControl, connecting the architectural extension and applications to prior work. The existing related-work framework and earlier cited works are retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and terminology corrections, updates the header and project link, renames Section 6.4 to Additional Applications, and reorganizes the appendices around a new SD3 section. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with new ablation plots, SD3.5 comparison and collection panels, a Gram-matrix plot, photographic and failure examples, and editing grids (Figures 13, 15–19 and 31–32). Original figure images are retained, while main-text Figures 6–8 are reordered and appendix displays are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through the reversed-ranking control and alternative style descriptor, and clarifies an applicability boundary with a concrete failure example. SD3.5 and photographic-style results broaden support, although these extensions are mainly qualitative and the principal benchmark and user study are unchanged. The evidence supports a limited overall gain in validation and clarity.
